review_comments.body:
** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Heavy lift** **Use the streamed `index` when ID-less tool-call updates arrive.** `_ToolCallIndexer` derives each index from the tool-call `id` alone. The Azure SDK model does not expose `index`. A delta without an `id` therefore takes the index of the latest call (`index_for`, lines 144-150). If one chunk contains ID-less argument updates for two calls, both updates receive the same index. A client that accumulates by index then appends both argument fragments to one call. The positional index used before this change kept them apart. The same merge can occur when ID-less updates for an earlier call arrive after a later call has opened. Where the raw payload provides the per-update `index`, the converter can use it as the accumulation key. The `id`-based logic can remain as a fallback when that index is absent.

This change fixes parallel streamed tool calls being merged under index 0 in Azure streaming. A remaining gap exists: if Azure sends argument updates without IDs for several calls in one chunk, those arguments can still be appended to the wrong call. That shape is unconfirmed, so the merge risk is modest, but the author should check it or use the raw per-update index where available.
